info.name: Campground POS API
info.description:
# Campground POS API

## How to use tokens
1. Open **0. Auth — Login by Role**
2. Run the login for the role you want (Owner / Staff / Customer / …)
3. Tests auto-save that role's token **and** set `active_token`
4. Most authenticated folders use `{{active_token}}` (collection auth)
5. Customer Portal folder forces `{{customer_token}}`; folder 6 (Super Admin) forces `{{superadmin_token}}`
6. Public Website folder uses **no auth**

## Roles
| Role | Typical use |
|------|-------------|
| owner | Location owner — POS + staff + map admin |
| admin | Location admin (create via Staff API) |
| staff | Day-to-day POS |
| customer | Guest portal |
| superadmin | SaaS platform — genuinely org-less, see folder 6 |

Update emails/passwords in collection variables or the companion environment.

## 2026-08-13 RBAC redesign
Folders 4/5 were split by actual role gate, not just by "staff vs admin" convention: folder 4 is now read/day-to-day-only (owner+admin+staff), folder 5 is management/deletion/GHL-sync actions (owner+admin only — several requests moved here from folder 4 on 2026-08-13, kept their names). Folder 6 (Super Admin) is genuinely org-less: it cannot reach any folder 4/5 endpoint (see folder 9's negative tests), and exists to list/block organizations and read (never write) across all of them. See `config/permissions.php` in the backend repo for the single source of truth this collection mirrors.

item.name: 0. Auth — Login by Role
item.description: Run a login to populate role tokens. Each login also sets active_token used by the rest of the collection.

request.description: Location owner. Saves owner_token + active_token.
Location admin (create via Staff Management first). Saves admin_token + active_token.
POS cashier/staff. Saves staff_token + active_token.
Customer portal. Account must be status=active. Saves customer_token + active_token.
SaaS superadmin — use after Super Admin folder work. Saves superadmin_token + active_token.
Uses collection auth {{active_token}}.
Generic register. Prefer Staff Management for real staff accounts.

request.description: Rate-limited: guest-browse (60/min/IP). Resolves tenant via OrganizationLocationResolver::resolveDefaultLocationId().
`{{product_id}}` here may be a Product id or a ProductRental id.
Gated only by the `email` query param matching the booking's customer email — not real auth.
Rate-limited: guest-booking (5/min/IP). Finds-or-creates the Customer and implicitly creates/links a customer portal account (verification email sent).
Only is_visible elements are included.

item.description: Unauthenticated browse/book widget. Matches the customer-facing website.

item.name: 2. Customer Account (register / verify)

request.description: Rate-limited: guest-register. Explicit self-service signup (separate from the implicit account creation on a public booking). Sends a verification email.
Same endpoint as staff login — saves the token into `customer_token` instead of `staff_token`.

Rate-limited: guest-verify. `token` comes from the verification email/link (set the `customer_action_token` collection variable manually from the email or dev log — it is never returned by any API response, by design).
Rate-limited: guest-resend-verification (5/hr per IP+email).
Requires the account to already be `verified` (see Customer Verify Code). Returns a JWT access token — signs the guest in immediately.
Rate-limited: guest-forgot-password (3/hr per IP+email).
`token` comes from the password-reset email link. Invalidates all existing JWT sessions on success.

item.description: Customer self-registration + verification. Paths are /customer/* (not /guest/*). Login saves customer_token.

item.name: 3. Customer Portal (role:customer)

request.description: Rate-limited: guest-change-password (10/min/user). Revokes all *other* sessions, keeps this one alive.
403s if the booking doesn't belong to this customer's linked customer.
422 if already cancelled or already paid (paid bookings must go through staff).
Updates the linked Customer record and re-syncs the GHL contact (non-blocking on failure).

item.description: Requires customer_token. Run Login as Customer first. Account must be active.

item.name: 4. POS Operations (owner / admin / staff)
item.description: Day-to-day POS. Uses {{active_token}} — login as Owner or Staff first.

request.description: Paginated. All query params optional/disabled by default — enable the ones you need.
find-or-create by email/phone within the tenant. Also implicitly creates/links a `role=customer` portal account for this email (no verification email sent when created by staff).
Bookable rentals only (product_rental_id not null). Local, fast — no live GHL calls.
Fetches live pricing/availability/duration from GHL via GhlRentalGateway (falls back to local-only payload if GHL is unreachable).
`product_id` accepts either a Product id or a ProductRental id (resolved via RentalResolver). Live GHL pricing — nothing persisted.

`payment_method`: omit (real GHL booking + invoice email, status `pending`) | `cash` (real booking, marked paid+confirmed immediately, no email) | `card` (Text2Pay link, status `requested`, same flow as customer bookings).
Self-heals GHL invoice/paid-status via GhlService::reconcileInvoiceStatus() before returning.
status: pending|confirmed|cancelled.
For a staff-visible 'requested' booking (e.g. a customer booking awaiting staff review): creates the real GHL calendar booking + invoice and emails the payment link.
Marks a cash 'pay later' booking as paid; self-heals a missing GHL calendar booking first if needed.

`items[].product_type`: rental|physical|addon. `payment_method`: cash|card. `payment_status`: paid|pending|draft. Used directly by staff for extras/add-ons; booking-linked rental transactions are normally auto-created by POST /bookings.
Setting to `paid` auto-sets invoice_status to completed and (for booking-linked transactions) triggers the GHL record-payment call.

item.name: Add Rental Marker to Map (admin only)

request.description: Example of placing a bookable rental as a map marker. `product_rental_id` here should be an actual ProductRental id, not a Product id.
Every field is independently optional/`sometimes` — PATCH only what changed (drag = x/y, resize = width/height, restyle = color/opacity, etc.).
Elements referencing this icon type fall back to the default pin rather than being deleted.
Requires client_id/client_secret already saved. Open the returned authorize_url in a browser to complete OAuth (redirects to /settings/engage/callback).

item.name: Engage OAuth Callback (browser redirect, not for direct use)

request.description: GHL redirects the browser here after the user authorizes — `code` and `state` (tenant_id) are supplied by GHL. Not meant to be called directly from Postman; kept here for completeness.
entity_type: customer|booking|product. `tenant_id` must be set explicitly — run Auth > Me first to populate the `tenant_id` collection variable.

item.description: Placeholder for SaaS-level routes. Login as Superadmin is already under Auth. Add platform routes here when built.

request.description: Same as Auth → Login as Superadmin.
Roles: superadmin only. Every other role -> 403 (proves super-admin is genuinely org-less: it's excluded from Tier 1 too).
Roles: superadmin only. Blocking is per-organization — a multi-org user keeps working under any other, non-blocked organization.
Read-only cross-org drill-down. Reuses ProductService::listServices() directly — does NOT run live GHL invoice reconciliation (unlike the staff Bookings/Product Transactions list endpoints).

Read-only — identifiers/status/token METADATA only, never access_token/refresh_token. This is the "Engage Identifiers only" view; Refresh Token / Data Sync are owner/admin-only actions super-admin cannot reach.
Roles: superadmin only now (moved off owner/admin — same controller method, gate changed). Folder default auth (superadmin_token) applies.

Open to any authenticated role (including customer) — the matrix has no secrets. Returns every {action, role, decider} triple plus the caller's own allowed-action list (data.self.allowed), which the frontend uses instead of hardcoded role checks.
No auth — GHL calls this directly. Example payload shown is for a contact.created event; opportunity.created/stage_changed events have a different shape (see GhlWebhookHandler).
